sections.h2: Which Fannin County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Valuation and billing live in different offices. Assessors decide what each parcel is worth and field exemption forms, and the Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment.

The Tax Commissioner's main office is at 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, Blue Ridge, GA 30513, on the same street as the courthouse. Call (706) 632-2645. The counter opens at 8:30 each weekday, closes at 5:00 Monday through Thursday, and closes at 4:30 on Friday. The Tax Assessor answers at (706) 632-5954, and the county links to an online parcel search on qPublic.

sections.h2: Fannin County homes and the mountain market
sections.html:
Fannin is a mountain county with a thin settlement pattern. A parcel here is often a few acres on a slope, so access roads, septic systems and well water show up in a buyer's questions early. The county posts ordinances that touch a sale, among them land development, building code enforcement, dilapidated buildings, manufactured homes and trailers, septic installation and short-term rentals. Read the ones that fit your property, and call the building department at (706) 632-8361 about a past permit.

About 26,111 people live in the county as of mid-2025. A typical owned home is valued at $306,600, median gross rent is $900 a month, and 78.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The county counts 19,655 housing units against 11,890 households, so a large share of the stock is not someone's year-round home. That fits the cabin and vacation market and explains why buyers ask about rental history and lodging tax records.

sections.h2: When is Fannin County property tax due?
sections.html:
Check your statement or call the Tax Commissioner for the due date, since Georgia lets each county pick its own. The Department of Revenue calls December 20 the default, with November 15, December 1 and installment billing as local alternatives.

Interest holds off for 60 days after the postmark on the statement, and penalties can follow on balances left open. Mobile homes run on their own track: apply for a location permit within 30 days of setting the home, then renew it between January 1 and April 1.

Inside Blue Ridge the city sends a second statement. City Hall says notices usually go out in November with a 60-day payment window counted from the postmark, and the mayor and council set the rate from values the county assessors produce. A Blue Ridge address therefore means two bills.

Returns are due between January 1 and April 1. Georgia treats silence as agreement: skip a return and last year's value carries forward.

  • Apply for homestead whenever you like during the year; the April 1 cutoff decides which tax year the exemption starts.
  • A missed application is treated as a waiver.
  • Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 before you go in.
  • Commercial and industrial inventory can be exempt under freeport if county voters adopted it; apply with the assessors during the return period.

New buyers should file for homestead after closing and keep a copy of the recorded deed ready. A seller's exemption does not follow the house, so the buyer files a separate application.

Mail the appeal to the Fannin County Board of Tax Assessors, postmarked no more than 45 days after the notice date. The notice itself carries the filing instructions.

An appeal challenges the fair market value on the notice. The amount of tax is not a ground. The assessors reread the file, and unresolved cases can reach the Board of Equalization and then Superior Court. Separately, anyone who paid tax that should never have been charged has three years from payment to ask in writing for a refund, and refunds tied to an appealed value are processed automatically once that value is final.

Owners of boats, aircraft or business equipment get a notice when the board rejects their return, and the same 45 days apply.

sections.h2: Short-term rentals when the house is sold
sections.html:
A short-term rental in unincorporated Fannin needs an annual lodging certificate, and a new owner cannot just keep using the seller's. The Lodging Division, at 400 West Main Street, Suite 100, lists the steps on its information page.

  • Complete the short-term rental application packet in full.
  • Email it with a PDF of the warranty deed, and wait until closing is done and the deed is in hand.
  • The county then sets up a portal account and emails instructions.
  • Buy the annual lodging certificate, which covers the current calendar year.
  • Report lodging tax each month, due by the 20th for the prior month's rentals.

An owner who uses Airbnb or VRBO to remit the monthly tax is still the one who enters the reporting amounts. If you sell a rental, give the buyer your recent monthly reports and ask the Lodging Division how the certificate transfers. The rental ordinance has been under revision, so ask the commissioners' office at 400 West Main Street, Suite 110, for the version in force before you advertise a house as a rental.

sections.h2: Selling with the tax bill in mind
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the Fannin County Tax Commissioner before the contract is final, because the closing attorney needs a figure and unpaid balances can pick up interest and penalties.

Spell out in the contract who covers the year's tax: values are set as of January 1, but the statement lands months later. If you hold a mortgage with escrow, tell your servicer about the sale so the escrow refund reaches you. The county also posts five-year tax digest history reports for 2017 through 2026 on its website, which help a buyer see how the levy has moved.

Intangible recording tax on a new mortgage is $1.50 for every $500 of face amount, and the security instrument is recorded within 90 days. If an inherited house has an estate in process, ask the probate court and the tax offices what papers they need before the deed is signed.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips on a mountain property
sections.html: A cash buyer does not wait on a lender appraisal, which can be slow on a remote parcel with a steep drive or private well. The tax steps do not go away. You still need the payoff, a clear record of any rental certificate, and the contract language on the year's bill. What drops out is the financing contingency, so the closing date depends on paperwork rather than on a bank's calendar.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Fannin County?
faqs.a: The Tax Commissioner mails statements and takes payment, while the Tax Assessors set values. Visit 400 West Main Street, Suite 103, in Blue Ridge, or call (706) 632-2645.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline for a Fannin County valuation?
faqs.a: Postmark a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the notice, addressed to the Board of Tax Assessors, and dispute the value shown.

faqs.q: Does the City of Blue Ridge send a separate tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. City Hall reports November mailings and a 60-day window from the postmark, and it relies on county values.

faqs.q: Can I list my Fannin County cabin as a short-term rental after buying it?
faqs.a: Only after you complete the county's application with the warranty deed and buy the annual lodging certificate. Wait until closing is finished and the deed is secured, then pay lodging tax by the 20th of each month.

faqs.q: How do I stop a homestead exemption from lapsing when I buy a Fannin County house?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Assessor at (706) 632-5954 for the form. File by April 1 of the first tax year you want covered, since a later application slips to the following year.
